stories.title: Van Nuys Apartments Trade for First Time Since Delivery
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 7203 Rubio Ave., a 30-unit multifamily property in the Lake Balboa neighborhood of Van Nuys. The property sold for $9.5 million or $316,667 per unit. Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC), a subsidiary of Marcus & Millichap, secured $6,223,000 in acquisition financing. “Bringing this property to market for the first time since its construction in 2013 generated significant investor interest,” said Neema Ahadian, senior managing director investments. “After a disciplined marketing process that included eight property tours and five competitive offers, we identified a qualified buyer who performed without requesting price reductions or credits in escrow. The transaction reflects continued demand for well-located, newer-vintage multifamily properties that are not subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.”  Ahadian and Leonardo Laterza, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Los Angeles office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, a local developer, and procured the buyer, a local private investor. Danny Abergel, executive managing director, capital markets, also based in the firm’s Los Angeles office, secured a five-year loan at 67% loan-to-value with a national bank on behalf of the buyer. Additional terms include a competitive interest rate and a 30-year amortization period. The post Van Nuys Apartments Trade for First Time Since Delivery appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 30-unit Van Nuys apartment sold for $9.5M ($316.7K/unit) after 11 years.
Property exempt from LA Rent Stabilization Ordinance; five competitive offers received.
MMCC financed $6.2M of $9.5M purchase; buyer is local private investor.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 7203 Rubio Ave., a 30-unit multifamily property in Lake Balboa, Van Nuys, for $9.5 million ($316,667 per unit). First trade since 2013 delivery generated eight tours and five competitive bids. Buyer, a local private investor, secured $6.2M in acquisition financing and did not request price reductions. The transaction signals sustained demand for newer, non-RSO-restricted apartments in LA's San Fernando Valley.
stories.impact: Strong pricing and multiple bids for post-2013 construction in Van Nuys despite restrictive rent-control environment indicate investor appetite for assets outside RSO jurisdiction. Developers should prioritize pre-RSO-exemption delivery timelines and Valley-submarket positioning to capture this capital flow.

stories.title: Williamsburg Mixed-Use Sale Completes “Round Trip” for Seller
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 235-237 Kent Ave., two mixed-use buildings in Brooklyn’s Williamsburg neighborhood, for $16.4 million. “We are happy to successfully complete a round trip for our seller, whom we previously sold the property for $12.3 million in 2021 during the pandemic,” said Shaun Riney of Marcus & Millichap in New York City. “The property is turnkey and located on the world-class corridor of Kent Avenue. The buyer was completing a 1031 exchange following the sale of a property in downtown Manhattan.” Riney, Michael Salvatico and Harrison Rich of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property on behalf of the seller. They also procured the buyer. Built in 1954, the buildings total 13,575 square feet and comprise 14 units, including 12 free-market two-bedroom apartments and two ground-floor commercial spaces. The commercial space is occupied by a restaurant and Ume Sushi. The post Williamsburg Mixed-Use Sale Completes “Round Trip” for Seller appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Williamsburg mixed-use building resold for $16.4M, up 33% from $12.3M in 2021.
14 units (12 free-market apartments, 2 commercial spaces) on Kent Avenue corridor.
Buyer completed 1031 exchange from downtown Manhattan disposition.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 235-237 Kent Ave., two mixed-use buildings in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, for $16.4 million—a 33% gain since 2021's pandemic-era $12.3M purchase. The 13,575-square-foot property comprises 14 units and two ground-floor retail spaces (restaurant, sushi bar). The buyer executed a 1031 exchange following a downtown Manhattan property sale.
stories.impact: The 33% price appreciation over three years and 1031 exchange activity signal strong investor confidence in Williamsburg's residential fundamentals and Kent Avenue's retail/mixed-use appeal. Multifamily developers should note robust demand for well-located, smaller-footprint mixed-use buildings with free-market apartments; 1031 capital is actively seeking such assets in established Brooklyn submarkets.

stories.title: Locally Based Investors Acquire Encinitas Offices from Family Trust
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield, along with locally based buyers DMJ Capital Partners, LLC and StoneSteps Real Estate, LLC, announced the acquisition of a multi-tenant office property, located at 169 Saxony Rd. in Encinitas, for $13.5 million. The property was previously held in a family trust, having been owned and operated by the seller and her late father for more than 24 years.The seller was represented by Brooks Campbell, Louay Alsadek, Peter Curry, and Maddie Mawby with Cushman & Wakefield. DMJ Capital Partners and StoneSteps Real Estate represented themselves. “As a sign of the strong investor demand for well-located office properties in San Diego, we received multiple offers from active investors,” said Campbell. Built in 2001, the two-story coastal office asset encompasses 40,270 rentable square feet and was 69% leased at the time of sale. Cushman & Wakefield has been appointed as leasing agent for the property. The post Locally Based Investors Acquire Encinitas Offices from Family Trust appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multi-tenant office sold in Encinitas for $13.5M; 69% leased at sale.
40,270 SF coastal property built 2001; held 24+ years by family trust.
Multiple competing bids received; Cushman & Wakefield appointed as leasing agent.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield announced the acquisition of 169 Saxony Rd., a multi-tenant office property in Encinitas, San Diego, for $13.5 million by local investors DMJ Capital Partners and StoneSteps Real Estate. The 40,270-square-foot asset, built in 2001 and owned by a family trust for 24+ years, was 69% leased at closing. Multiple offers from active investors were received.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Story confirms strong demand for well-located coastal office assets in San Diego, but office market appetite does not directly affect apartment supply or demand dynamics. If you monitor potential San Diego office-to-residential conversion opportunities (zoning permitting), note that coastal Encinitas office commanded premium pricing, signaling limited redevelopment upside vs. office hold.

stories.title: First Project Under NYS Housing Acceleration Fund Closes on Financing
stories.excerpt: New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) Commissioner RuthAnne Visnauskas announced that the first project under the Housing Acceleration Fund launched last year has closed on construction financing. North White Plains, a $178-million mixed-use transit-oriented development in Westchester County and located directly across from the North White Plains Metro-North Station, will feature 296 mixed-income apartments, retail and publicly accessible open space. The fund provides self-sustaining loans to shovel-ready housing projects. “By providing low-cost financing for mixed-income housing projects, we are jumpstarting construction of new apartments that will benefit families, seniors, young adults, and those looking for a modern place to live,” saidVisnauskas. Funding tincludes $120.6 million from Merchants Capital, $18 million from the Housing Acceleration Fund, $10 million from The Community Preservation Corporation, and $29.7 million in equity from Basis Investment Group and BRP Companies. Developed by BRP Companies, North White Plains will include a mix of studios, one-bedroom and two-bedroom residences. Thirty apartments will be designated as affordable housing. The post First Project Under NYS Housing Acceleration Fund Closes on Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: North White Plains TOD closes $178M construction financing; 296 mixed-income apartments.
$120.6M from Merchants Capital, $18M Housing Acceleration Fund, $29.7M equity.
Transit-oriented across from Metro-North station; 30 units designated affordable.
stories.summary: New York State HCR announced the first project under the Housing Acceleration Fund closed construction financing. North White Plains, a $178-million transit-oriented development in Westchester County across from North White Plains Metro-North Station, will deliver 296 mixed-income apartments, retail, and public space. Financing includes $120.6M senior debt (Merchants Capital), $18M Housing Acceleration Fund loan, $10M Community Preservation Corp, and $29.7M equity (Basis/BRP).
stories.impact: HAF demonstrates NYS willingness to provide below-market subordinate debt to accelerate mixed-income multifamily in TOD locations. Developers in Westchester and downstate NY should investigate HAF eligibility for shovel-ready projects; low-cost financing layering (HAF + tax credits for 30 affordable units) improves underwriting on transit-proximate development and signals state preference for transit-oriented infill over sprawl.

stories.title: R.W. Holmes Tapped to Lease Former National Amusements Headquarters in Norwood
stories.excerpt: R.W. Holmes Commercial Real Estate has been retained as leasing agent for 846 University Ave., a Class A office property in Norwood, MA. Previously the headquarters of National Amusements and Showcase Cinemas, the property is now being marketed for lease for the first time since 2006. “Today’s tenants are looking for quality, accessibility, and a great value that will support their business and employees,” said Michael Fahy, assistant VP at R.W. Holmes. “846 University Ave. delivers on all three, making it an outstanding opportunity for companies looking to establish or expand their presence in the heart of the 128 south market.” The property is under new ownership, Falconi Properties, as of May 2026 with major improvements now underway. According to R.W. Holmes, it offers flexible leasing opportunities for office, medical, and Flex/R&D users, with suites ranging from approximately 4,000 square feet to a full-building 60,000 square feet. The post R.W. Holmes Tapped to Lease Former National Amusements Headquarters in Norwood appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Former National Amusements HQ in Norwood, MA now leasing after 2006.
60,000 SF Class A office; under new ownership (Falconi Properties) as May 2026.
Flexible suites (4K–60K SF) for office, medical, Flex/R&D uses.
stories.summary: R.W. Holmes Commercial Real Estate was retained as leasing agent for 846 University Ave., a Class A office property in Norwood, MA, previously the headquarters of National Amusements and Showcase Cinemas. The 60,000-square-foot building was acquired by Falconi Properties as of May 2026, with major improvements underway. The property is being marketed for the first time since 2006, offering flexible suite sizes (4,000–60,000 SF) for office, medical, and Flex/R&D tenants.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Office repositioning in Boston's Route 128 south corridor does not directly affect apartment demand or supply. If Norwood zoning permits adaptive reuse to mixed-use or residential, note that a prominent office vacancy (off-market for 20 years) could present conversion opportunity, but no redevelopment signal is present.

stories.title: Spanish Hotel Operator Buys Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street for $95M
stories.excerpt: A 107-key hotel in Midtown has traded for roughly $95 million. Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish hotel chain managing more than 300 properties globally, has purchased the Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street from Azora, another Spanish company specializing in large-scale hotel investments, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Eastdil Secured’s Jeffrey Davis and Scott Ellman arranged the deal for the seller, while it was unclear who repped the buyer. Eastdil declined to comment, while spokespeople for Eurostars and Azora did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The Real Deal first reported the news. It’s unclear when Azora acquired the 14-story hotel a block south of Grand Central Terminal, but the last trade recorded in property records was in 2007, when hotel chain Grupo Hotusa and Losan Hotels bought it for $77 million. Eurostars, which also owns the Eurostars Wall Street hotel at 129 Front Street in the Financial District, is a subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa, so the Midtown property is returning to its previous roots. The property was built around 1910, but not as a hotel. The building was originally the site of the historic headquarters of the Chemists’ Club, a prominent social and dining hub for leading scientists and industry pioneers. The building was later redeveloped by fortuna realty group in 1997 and opened in 2000 as the Dylan Hotel. Last year, it was again heavily redesigned and rebranded, and officially opened as the Chemists’ Club Hotel. The hotel is currently home to Benjamin Steakhouse on the ground floor and features amenities such as a lounge bar, coworking spaces and a fitness center. News of the sale comes after a slew of other hotel sales in Manhattan recently. In June, Meliá Hotels International bought the 12-story hotel at 132-142 West 27th Street in NoMad for $203 million, while Omni Lifestyle Living acquired a Marriott hotel at 21 West 37th Street in Midtown for $39.9 million, also in June. bullets: Eurostars Hotel Company (Spain) buys Chemists' Club Hotel NYC for $95M.
107-key Midtown hotel; 14-story, built ~1910, located 1 block south GCT.
Eurostars subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa; property returns to previous owner's roots (2007).
stories.summary: Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish operator managing 300+ properties globally, purchased the Chemists' Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street for approximately $95 million. The 107-key Midtown property, built around 1910, is located one block south of Grand Central Terminal. Eurostars is a subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa, which previously owned the asset in 2007 when it traded for $77 million.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Story indicates continued foreign capital interest in premium NYC hospitality assets, but does not signal changes in apartment demand, supply, or financing. If considering hotel-to-residential conversion in Midtown, note that Class A hospitality assets remain investable at scale, reducing likelihood of near-term conversion pressure.

stories.title: Izo Capital Lends $26M on Wyoming Apartments Near Jackson Hole
stories.excerpt: Sundance Properties has sealed $25.6 million of construction financing to bring a multifamily development in Alpine, Wyo., across the finish line, Commercial Observer has learned. Izo Capital supplied the 24-month senior construction loan to fund the completion of Phase 1 of the developer’s planned the Flats at Alpine Junction project comprising 64 units. The debt will support the completion of three additional buildings comprising 48 apartments on top of 16 units that are already completed and leased. Peter Porraro, co-founder and chief investment officer at Izo Capital, said the overall project, which will eventually total 160 units, is set up for success given that it’s 35 miles from Jackson Hole mountain valley, with a number of employers based in the town of Jackson, Wyo. Porraro noted that Alpine also has demand drivers for multifamily with limited supply coupled with a newly opened medical center and a public charter school scheduled to open for the 2026-2027 academic year. “It’s very hard to develop out there, and it’s hard to get the infrastructure,” Porraro told CO of the need for more apartments projects near Jackson Hole. “There’s just no supply and nothing new in the market.” The Flats development has already shown strong leasing momentum, according to Porraro, with the current rental rates helping support underwriting assumptions in the loan for the remaining phases of the project. The first phase is slated for completion next spring. Porraro noted that there is large-scale demand for rental housing for those who work in Jackson Hole given that median home prices in the city are close to $3 million, with townhomes starting at around $1 million. He said the project at 303 Highway also benefits from transportation connectivity that includes direct access to the START Bus system linking Alpine and Jackson. “The demand we’ve experienced from the first completed building reinforces the critical need for new rental housing in Alpine,”
bullets: Sundance Properties secures $25.6M construction loan for 64-unit Phase 1 (Alpine, WY).
Flats at Alpine Junction will total 160 units; 16 already complete and leased.
Izo Capital 24-month senior loan; Jackson Hole proximity (35 mi), new medical center, charter school 2026-27 drive demand.
stories.summary: Izo Capital provided $25.6 million in 24-month senior construction financing to Sundance Properties to complete Phase 1 of the Flats at Alpine Junction in Alpine, Wyoming. Phase 1 comprises 64 units (16 complete and leased, 48 under construction); the full project will total 160 units. Demand drivers include proximity to Jackson Hole (35 miles), local employers, a newly opened medical center, and a public charter school scheduled to open for 2026–2027.
stories.impact: Limited supply, nascent job growth around Jackson Hole, and new institutional anchors (medical center, school) create runway for multifamily absorption in underserved Alpine submarket. Developers should monitor Jackson Hole area employment expansion and education/healthcare facility openings as leading indicators for secondary mountain-resort multifamily demand; construction financing availability (Izo Capital's involvement) suggests lender comfort with supply-constrained Alpine plays.

stories.title: CW Realty Closes Deal to Buy 55 Smith Street in Downtown Brooklyn for $58M
stories.excerpt: CW Realty Group closed on a deal to acquire a parking facility in Downtown Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. Cheskie Weisz’ CW Realty entered into a contract to purchase 55 Smith Street in December from New Jersey-based firm Edison Properties, Crain’s New York Business reported at the time. The sale closed on Friday and its price was disclosed at $58 million, according to broker JLL. CW Realty has not disclosed any specifics about their plans for the site, which has an alternative address of 160 Livingston Street, but the lot spans 13,707 square feet and is one of the biggest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn, the JLL Capital Markets team said. “This transaction demonstrates the strength of demand for well-located development opportunities across New York City, particularly in neighborhoods with strong residential fundamentals and supportive zoning,” JLL’s Mike Mazzara, who negotiated the deal alongside Ethan Stanton, Brendan Maddigan and Drew Isaacson, said in a statement. “The site offers a combination of scale, flexibility and development incentives in one of Brooklyn’s most dynamic neighborhoods.” CW Realty and Edison Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Developers can build 137,000 square feet on the site as of right or 164,000 square feet under the Universal Affordability Preference program with no height limits or parking requirements for a potential housing development. CW Realty has the option to build using the city’s 485-x program and benefit from reforms made under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity. An added bonus is that development on the site is not restricted to rental housing or condominiums, according to JLL. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CW Realty closes $58M acquisition of 55 Smith Street (160 Livingston), Downtown Brooklyn.
13,707 SF parking facility; described as one of biggest residential dev'mt opportunities in downtown.
Deal signals demand for large, flexible development sites in Brooklyn with supportive zoning.
stories.summary: CW Realty Group closed acquisition of 55 Smith Street (alternative address: 160 Livingston Street) in Downtown Brooklyn for $58 million. The 13,707-square-foot parcel—one of the largest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn—is a former parking facility. JLL described the site as offering scale, flexibility, and development incentives with strong neighborhood residential fundamentals and supportive zoning.
stories.impact: Major land assemblage in Downtown Brooklyn at premium valuation signals continued institutional investor appetite for large, shovel-ready residential development sites. Nearby multifamily developers should expect intensified competition for remaining assemblage opportunities and upward pressure on Downtown Brooklyn land pricing. Zoning support and strong residential demand justify aggressive acquisition pricing; monitor CW Realty's entitlement timeline and unit count target to gauge market absorption expectations.

stories.title: Kimco Buys Two Broward Retail Centers for $109M
stories.excerpt: Kimco Realty, one of the biggest owners of grocery-anchored retail centers in the country, has acquired two more in Broward County for a combined $109 million from KPR Centers, property records show. In the largest transaction, the Jericho, N.Y.-based REIT paid $56 million for Sunshine Plaza, a 245,744-square-foot property between 4017 and 4299 West Commercial Boulevard in Tamarac, just east of the Florida’s Turnpike. Publix and Marshalls anchor the 19-acre shopping center. Other tenants include Crunch Fitness, Krispy Kreme and Subway. New York-based KPR had purchased the property for $28.5 million in 2014. In the smaller trade, Kimco Realty paid $53 million for the 254,749-square-foot Pompano Marketplace at 1115 and 1117 South Federal Highway. It also spans about 19 acres, with a Walmart Neighborhood Market as the anchor. Other tenants include Ross Dress for Less, Carrabba’s Italian Grill and TD Bank. KPR Centers had purchased the asset for $46.8 million in 2015. Kimco Realty owns 589 properties nationwide, including 44 across South Florida. In one of South Florida’s largest retail deals in recent years, the REIT paid $216 million for The Shops at Mary Brickell Village in Miami in 2022. Representatives for Kimco Realty and KPR Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kimco Realty acquires two Broward retail centers from KPR Centers for $109M total.
Sunshine Plaza (Tamarac): $56M, 245.7K SF, Publix/Marshalls anchors; Pompano Marketplace: $53M, 254.7K SF, Walmart anchor.
Kimco now owns 589 properties; purchases reflect REIT consolidation of grocery-anchored centers in South Florida.
stories.summary: Kimco Realty, a major U.S. REIT, acquired two grocery-anchored retail centers in Broward County from KPR Centers for a combined $109 million. Sunshine Plaza in Tamarac (245,744 SF, Publix/Marshalls) sold for $56 million; Pompano Marketplace (254,749 SF, Walmart Neighborhood Market) sold for $53 million. Both properties span approximately 19 acres and were previous KPR acquisitions from 2014–2015.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Story reflects continued REIT appetite for grocery-anchored retail in South Florida, but does not signal changes to apartment demand, supply, or financing. If considering mixed-use development with ground-floor retail in Broward, note that Kimco's active acquisition of grocery-anchored centers suggests strong demand for necessity-based retail; partnering retail tenants or outparcels may be more feasible than previously thought.

stories.title: Schuckman Buys Northeast Queens Shopping Center for $56M
stories.excerpt: Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million. BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, purchased the Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway, according to a deed transfer in property records filed Friday. The purchase could be a play for assets tied to grocery stores and other necessity-based retail. Schuckman’s brokerage firm, Schuckman Realty, will handle leasing for the shopping center, according to the buyer. Acadia Realty Trust provided about $48.5 million in financing to Schuckman for the acquisition through a shell corporation, with Acadia’s Chief Financial Officer John Gottfried signing the mortgage documents. Punia & Marx and Acadia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Punia & Marx has owned the property since at least 1975, and the amount paid for that acquisition is unknown. Schuckman seems to have been involved in the management operations of the 220,000-square-foot shopping center, which is also leased to a Chase Bank branch, with a 2020 flier listing Kenneth Schuckman and Jessica Vilmenay as exclusive brokers. The advertisement said at the time that a redevelopment of the property would be taking place, but was not specific about the nature of the repositioning. Schuckman promoted the center based on 100,000 cars passing by the center daily on the Cross Island Parkway and 333,000 people living within three miles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BTF Capital (Schuckman/Malinsky) acquires Whitestone Shopping Center (Queens) for $56M.
220K SF, Key Food-anchored; Acadia Realty Trust provided $48.5M financing; Punia & Marx owned since ~1975.
Schuckman Realty handles leasing; grocery/necessity retail play in northeast Queens.
stories.summary: BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, acquired the Whitestone Shopping Center in northeast Queens for $56 million. The 220,000-square-foot, Key Food-anchored property is located at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway. Acadia Realty Trust provided approximately $48.5 million in acquisition financing. Punia & Marx, the previous owner, had held the asset since at least 1975. Schuckman Realty was appointed as leasing agent.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Story reflects investor focus on grocery-anchored necessity-retail consolidation in outer boroughs; does not signal apartment demand or supply shifts. If evaluating mixed-use or residential development in northeast Queens, note that retail capital remains strong for Key Food-anchored centers, potentially limiting conversion upside; focus acquisitions on non-grocery-anchored retail sites or pure land parcels.
